review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

4:1.sourceText: Ὡς οὖν ἔγνω ὁ Κύριος ὅτι ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὅτι Ἰησοῦς πλείονας μαθητὰς ποιεῖ καὶ βαπτίζει ἢ Ἰωάνης,
4:1.targetText: When Jesus realized that the Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John

groups.note: ἤκουσαν ("had heard") is rendered were aware.
BSB has just named Jesus, so the repeated name is rendered He.
ποιεῖ ("makes") is rendered was gaining.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
BSB follows a different reading here; its English names Jesus where N1904 has ὁ Κύριος ("the Lord").
BSB leaves this second ὅτι ("that") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with a different word here; N1904 has ὁ Κύριος ("the Lord").

4:2.sourceText: —καίτοιγε Ἰησοῦς αὐτὸς οὐκ ἐβάπτιζεν ἀλλ’ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ,—
4:2.targetText: (although it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples),

unmappedSource.reason: The intensive αὐτός ("himself") is not rendered separately.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English cleft construction (it was … who) for emphasis.
Part of the English cleft construction (it was … who).

4:3.sourceText: ἀφῆκεν τὴν Ἰουδαίαν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
4:3.targetText: He left Judea and returned to Galilee.

groups.note: ἀπῆλθεν πάλιν ("went away again") is rendered returned.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:4.sourceText: Ἔδει δὲ αὐτὸν διέρχεσθαι διὰ τῆς Σαμαρίας.
4:4.targetText: Now He had to pass through Samaria.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:5.sourceText: ἔρχεται οὖν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρίας λεγομένην Συχὰρ, πλησίον τοῦ χωρίου ὃ ἔδωκεν Ἰακὼβ Ἰωσὴφ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ·
4:5.targetText: So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The dative τῷ υἱῷ ("to the son") supplies to; the name Joseph does not decline.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:6.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πηγὴ τοῦ Ἰακώβ. ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς κεκοπιακὼς ἐκ τῆς ὁδοιπορίας ἐκαθέζετο οὕτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ· ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη.
4:6.targetText: Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

groups.note: τοῦ marks the genitive of the indeclinable name Ἰακώβ.
BSB turns "There was Jacob's well …; so Jesus … sat" into a since-clause, so the inferential οὖν is rendered Since.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves οὕτως ("just as He was") untranslated.

4:7.sourceText: ἔρχεται γυνὴ ἐκ τῆς Σαμαρίας ἀντλῆσαι ὕδωρ. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Δός μοι πεῖν.
4:7.targetText: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”

groups.note: ἐκ τῆς Σαμαρίας ("from Samaria") is rendered by the adjective Samaritan; the name is spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB joins the two clauses, which have no connective in Greek, with When.

4:8.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπεληλύθεισαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἵνα τροφὰς ἀγοράσωσιν.
4:8.targetText: (His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB marks the explanatory γάρ with parentheses instead of a word.

4:9.sourceText: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ Σαμαρεῖτις Πῶς σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὢν παρ’ ἐμοῦ πεῖν αἰτεῖς γυναικὸς Σαμαρείτιδος οὔσης; οὐ γὰρ συνχρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρείταις.
4:9.targetText: “You are a Jew,” said the woman. “How can You ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)

groups.note: The participle ὤν ("being") is rendered as the statement You are a Jew.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν untranslated.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.
BSB does not repeat ἡ Σαμαρεῖτις ("the Samaritan") with the speaker; her own question calls her a Samaritan woman.
BSB's apposition (me, a Samaritan woman) leaves οὔσης ("being") unexpressed.

4:10.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Εἰ ᾔδεις τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ λέγων σοι Δός μοι πεῖν, σὺ ἂν ᾔτησας αὐτὸν καὶ ἔδωκεν ἄν σοι ὕδωρ ζῶν.
4:10.targetText: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb answered.
ὁ λέγων … Δός ("the one saying, Give") is rendered asking … for: BSB turns the quoted request into indirect speech.
ἄν with the aorist marks the unreal result, would have.
ἄν with the aorist marks the unreal result, would have.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῇ ("to her") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB's indirect wording (asking you for a drink) leaves μοι ("me") unexpressed.

4:11.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε, οὔτε ἄντλημα ἔχεις καὶ τὸ φρέαρ ἐστὶν βαθύ· πόθεν οὖν ἔχεις τὸ ὕδωρ τὸ ζῶν;
4:11.targetText: “Sir,” the woman replied, “You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. Where then will You get this living water?

groups.note: The negative οὔτε with ἄντλημα ("a bucket") is rendered You have nothing to draw with.
ἔχεις ("do you have") is rendered will You get.
The article τό points to the water just mentioned and is rendered this.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with two extra words here that name the speaker; N1904 has no subject.

4:12.sourceText: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰακώβ, ὃς ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν τὸ φρέαρ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔπιεν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ θρέμματα αὐτοῦ;
4:12.targetText: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?”

groups.note: The article τό points to the well they stand by and is rendered this.
The verb is understood again with the sons and livestock; BSB repeats it as did.
καί ("and") adds the sons and livestock and is rendered as (as did his sons).

unmappedSource.reason: μή only marks a question expecting the answer no; English has a plain question.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:13.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Πᾶς ὁ πίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος τούτου διψήσει πάλιν·
4:13.targetText: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb said.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's drinks this water leaves the partitive ἐκ ("from") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:14.sourceText: ὃς δ’ ἂν πίῃ ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος οὗ ἐγὼ δώσω αὐτῷ, οὐ μὴ διψήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ τὸ ὕδωρ ὃ δώσω αὐτῷ γενήσεται ἐν αὐτῷ πηγὴ ὕδατος ἁλλομένου εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
4:14.targetText: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”

groups.note: ὃς ἄν ("whoever") works as one unit.
οὐ μή … εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("not … forever") is rendered never.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's drinks the water leaves the partitive ἐκ ("from") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ("which") unexpressed.

4:15.sourceText: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνή Κύριε, δός μοι τοῦτο τὸ ὕδωρ, ἵνα μὴ διψῶ μηδὲ διέρχωμαι ἐνθάδε ἀντλεῖν.
4:15.targetText: The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.”

groups.note: μηδέ ("nor") is rendered and; the negative not carries over.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:16.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ Ὕπαγε φώνησον τὸν ἄνδρα σου καὶ ἐλθὲ ἐνθάδε.
4:16.targetText: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”

groups.note: ἐνθάδε ("here") is rendered back.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek has only λέγει ("He says").

4:17.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ἡ γυνὴ καὶ εἶπεν Οὐκ ἔχω ἄνδρα. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Καλῶς εἶπες ὅτι Ἄνδρα οὐκ ἔχω·
4:17.targetText: “I have no husband,” the woman replied.  Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb replied.
Καλῶς εἶπες ("you said well") is rendered You are correct to say; same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula for BSB's wording You are correct.

4:18.sourceText: πέντε γὰρ ἄνδρας ἔσχες, καὶ νῦν ὃν ἔχεις οὐκ ἔστιν σου ἀνήρ· τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἴρηκας.
4:18.targetText: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”

groups.note: The relative ὅν ("whom") is rendered the man.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this") unexpressed.

4:19.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή Κύριε, θεωρῶ ὅτι προφήτης εἶ σύ.
4:19.targetText: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.

4:20.sourceText: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ προσεκύνησαν· καὶ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐστὶν ὁ τόπος ὅπου προσκυνεῖν δεῖ.
4:20.targetText: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”

groups.note: The impersonal δεῖ ("it is necessary") is rendered one must.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB makes clear that the plural ὑμεῖς ("you") means the Jews.
English supplies a general subject for the impersonal δεῖ.

4:21.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πίστευέ μοι, γύναι, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὔτε ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ οὔτε ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις προσκυνήσετε τῷ Πατρί.
4:21.targetText: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῇ ("to her") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ὅτι ("that") unexpressed.

4:22.sourceText: ὑμεῖς προσκυνεῖτε ὃ οὐκ οἴδατε, ἡμεῖς προσκυνοῦμεν ὃ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι ἡ σωτηρία ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐστίν·
4:22.targetText: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:23.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν, ὅτε οἱ ἀληθινοὶ προσκυνηταὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ Πατρὶ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ· καὶ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ τοιούτους ζητεῖ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτόν·
4:23.targetText: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.

groups.note: ἐστιν ("is [here]") with νῦν is rendered has now come.
καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered for.
τοιούτους ("such people") is rendered such as these.
The article with the participle ("those who worship") is rendered to worship.

4:24.sourceText: Πνεῦμα ὁ Θεός, καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ δεῖ προσκυνεῖν.
4:24.targetText: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

groups.note: The article with the participle ("those who worship") is rendered His worshipers.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none.
BSB follows a reading with an extra word here, rendered Him; N1904 has no object.

4:25.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή Οἶδα ὅτι Μεσσίας ἔρχεται, ὁ λεγόμενος Χριστός· ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν ἅπαντα.
4:25.targetText: The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When He comes, He will explain everything to us.”

groups.note: The article with the participle ("the one called") is rendered called.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.

4:26.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι, ὁ λαλῶν σοι.
4:26.targetText: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.”

groups.note: The article with the participle ("the one speaking") is rendered who speak.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῇ ("to her") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a predicate; Ἐγώ εἰμι ("I am") has none.

4:27.sourceText: Καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἦλθαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ὅτι μετὰ γυναικὸς ἐλάλει· οὐδεὶς μέντοι εἶπεν Τί ζητεῖς ἢ τί λαλεῖς μετ’ αὐτῆς;
4:27.targetText: Just then His disciples returned and were surprised that He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”

groups.note: ἐπὶ τούτῳ ("at this") is rendered Just then.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; εἶπεν has none in Greek.
English supplies from her; the Greek has μετ’ αὐτῆς ("with her") only with the second question.

4:28.sourceText: ἀφῆκεν οὖν τὴν ὑδρίαν αὐτῆς ἡ γυνὴ καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις
4:28.targetText: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people,

groups.note: The dative τοῖς ἀνθρώποις supplies to.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB lists the actions with a comma instead of and.

4:29.sourceText: Δεῦτε ἴδετε ἄνθρωπον ὃς εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα· μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός;
4:29.targetText: “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?”

groups.note: The question particle μήτι (expecting no) is rendered Could.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the relative pronoun ἅ ("which") unexpressed.

4:30.sourceText: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτόν.
4:30.targetText: So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English left.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds So; the Greek has no connective here.

4:31.sourceText: Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες Ῥαββεί, φάγε.
4:31.targetText: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.”

groups.note: Ἐν τῷ μεταξύ ("in the meantime") is rendered Meanwhile.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγοντες ("saying") introducing the quotation is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; φάγε has none in Greek.

4:32.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε.
4:32.targetText: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
οὐκ οἴδατε ("you do not know") is rendered you know nothing about.

4:33.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ πρὸς ἀλλήλους Μή τις ἤνεγκεν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν;
4:33.targetText: So the disciples asked one another, “Could someone have brought Him food?”

groups.note: The question particle μή (expecting no) is rendered Could.
φαγεῖν ("to eat") is rendered food.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's asked takes one another directly; πρός ("to") has no separate word.

4:34.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με καὶ τελειώσω αὐτοῦ τὸ ἔργον.
4:34.targetText: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has another form of the same verb here.
The article with the participle ("of the one who sent") is rendered of Him who sent.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:35.sourceText: οὐχ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Ἔτι τετράμηνός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται; ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας, ὅτι λευκαί εἰσιν πρὸς θερισμόν. ἤδη
4:35.targetText: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered until: four months, and the harvest comes.
λευκαί ("white") is rendered ripe.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB marks the quotation with quotation marks instead of ὅτι.
BSB's until-phrase leaves ἔρχεται ("comes") unexpressed.
BSB leaves ἰδού ("behold") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

sourceMoved.reason: N1904 prints ἤδη ("already") at the end of 4:35; BSB renders it Already at the start of 4:36.

4:36.sourceText: ὁ θερίζων μισθὸν λαμβάνει καὶ συνάγει καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων.
4:36.targetText: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.

groups.note: N1904 prints ἤδη at the end of 4:35.
The article with the participle ("the one reaping") is rendered the reaper.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a possessive; the Greek has none.

4:37.sourceText: ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ ὁ λόγος ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὅτι ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ σπείρων καὶ ἄλλος ὁ θερίζων.
4:37.targetText: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.

groups.note: The article with the participle ("the one sowing") is rendered sows.
The article with the participle ("the one reaping") is rendered reaps.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB marks the saying with quotation marks instead of ὅτι.
BSB turns "one is the sower" into "One sows", so this ἐστίν has no separate word.

4:38.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς θερίζειν ὃ οὐχ ὑμεῖς κεκοπιάκατε· ἄλλοι κεκοπιάκασιν, καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν κόπον αὐτῶν εἰσεληλύθατε.
4:38.targetText: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.”

groups.note: εἰσεληλύθατε ("you have entered into") is rendered have taken up.

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English taken up.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds now to mark the contrast.

4:39.sourceText: Ἐκ δὲ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν Σαμαρειτῶν διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς γυναικὸς μαρτυρούσης ὅτι Εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα.
4:39.targetText: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony, “He told me everything I ever did.”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered Jesus.
The partitive genitive supplies of; same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
τὸν λόγον … μαρτυρούσης ("the word … testifying") is rendered testimony.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB marks the quotation with quotation marks instead of ὅτι.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ἅ ("which") unexpressed.

4:40.sourceText: ὡς οὖν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Σαμαρεῖται, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν μεῖναι παρ’ αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ δύο ἡμέρας.
4:40.targetText: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days.

groups.note: Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἐκεῖ ("there") untranslated.

4:41.sourceText: καὶ πολλῷ πλείους ἐπίστευσαν διὰ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ,
4:41.targetText: And many more believed because of His message.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:42.sourceText: τῇ τε γυναικὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὐκέτι διὰ τὴν σὴν λαλιὰν πιστεύομεν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκηκόαμεν, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ Σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου.
4:42.targetText: They said to the woman, “We now believe not only because of your words; we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.”

groups.note: The dative τῇ γυναικί supplies to.
Οὐκέτι ("no longer") is rendered We now believe not only.
